title: Advanced Econometrics-I
description:
Topic list taken from **7th Semester (FINAL SYLLABUS)**. Seven blocks, each with a Wooldridge chapter reference and a slide deck.

The through-line of the whole course is **identification**: every block is another answer to the question *what has to be true before this regression coefficient means what I want it to mean?* IV answers it with an exclusion restriction, panel methods with a within-transformation, Heckman with a selection equation, PSM with unconfoundedness, DiD with parallel trends. Learn the assumption behind each, and the exam takes care of itself.

> Two different Wooldridge books are cited. **CH 5, 6, 15, 16 (Cross Section)** means *Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data*; **CH 14, 16 (Introductory)** means *Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach*. Do not mix up the chapter numbers between them.

Record the real structure here so mock papers match it.

chapters.title: Instrumental Variables and 2SLS
chapters.ref: Wooldridge, Cross Section, Ch. 5–6 · Slide: Instrumental Variable and 2SLS
chapters.summary: Instrumental variable · IV derivation · IV estimator · two-stage least squares · testing endogeneity · identification · overidentifying restrictions · weak instruments · partial F statistic.

chapters.title: Nonlinear Models
chapters.ref: Wooldridge, Cross Section, Ch. 15–16 · Slide: Nonlinear Models
chapters.summary: Linear probability model · logit and probit · maximum likelihood estimation · goodness of fit · multinomial logit (MNL) · ordered probit/logit · Tobit.

chapters.title: Introduction to Panel Data
chapters.ref: Wooldridge, Introductory, Ch. 14 · Slide: The Data
chapters.summary: Panel data model · fixed effects · dummy variable regression · first differencing · random effects · FD vs FE · FE vs RE.

chapters.title: Heckman Selection Correction Model
chapters.summary: Sample selection as an omitted-variable problem; the inverse Mills ratio; the two-step estimator.

chapters.title: Treatment Selection: Propensity Score Matching
chapters.summary: The treatment selection problem; matching on the propensity score; common support and balance.

chapters.title: Difference in Differences
chapters.summary: The 2×2 design, the parallel-trends assumption, and the interaction-term regression that implements it.

chapters.title: Simultaneous Equations
chapters.ref: Wooldridge, Introductory, Ch. 16 · Slide: Simultaneous Equation
chapters.summary: Simultaneity bias · identification (order and rank conditions) · systems of equations.

textbooks.title: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data
textbooks.author: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge
textbooks.chaptersCovered: Ch. 5–6 (IV and 2SLS), Ch. 15–16 (binary, multinomial and censored response)
textbooks.notes: The syllabus's *"(Cross Section)"* citations point here. This is the graduate text — matrix notation throughout, and it proves what the introductory book asserts. Use it when a question says *derive* or *show that*.

textbooks.title: Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach
textbooks.author: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge
textbooks.notes: The syllabus's *"(Introductory)"* citations. Far gentler, and its worked examples are the ones most likely to be recycled into exam questions. Confirm the edition — chapter numbers are stable across recent editions but section numbers move.
